span.label: **THE STAGED SOURCE IS A DAMAGED 1951 SCAN, AND UNTIL NOW THE RECORD DID NOT SAY SO.** The OCR fails at the LETTER level, not merely at diacritics: `The! CXISTL·NCC o( K. S. LA~HLEY` is `existence` with `c` substituted for `e` twice and a stray interpunct, inside a sentence that also carries `11cr\'ous systl•m` for `nervous system`. **67 tokens of 16,563 whitespace-delimited words carry a stray symbol between two letters** (terminal-a's predicate, one or more letters either side); 34 on the stricter two-letter form. [CORRECTED 2026-08-23: this sentence continued `CLAUDE_B counts 99 of 12,271 on a stricter pattern and a different tokenisation`, kept here verbatim because it was published. Wrong twice over - CLAUDE_B WITHDREW the 99 as a LOOSE pattern counting one-letter fragments, so it was not the stricter one, and I repeated their number without running their predicate. Their corrected figure is 27 of 12,271, 0.22%, against my 34 of 16,523 alphabetic tokens, 0.21%.] Both describe the same paper. **No accent table or render-time map reaches this class** - the characters are wrong, not misplaced

span.label: **THE ARGUMENT IN ONE SENTENCE, AND IT TURNS ON A PROPERTY OF THE ELEMENTS:** `Quotation withheld` If an element carries no information about what follows it, then no amount of association between elements can produce an order. **The refutation is not empirical, it is about what associations are able to encode** - which is why it has survived seventy-five years of contrary data
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE STRONGEST FORM OF IT IS THE SYNTAX CLAIM:** `Quotation withheld` Not in the words - so it is not associative. Not in the idea - so it is not simply read off the meaning either. **Both of the obvious places to put it are refused in one sentence**, which leaves ordering as a separate mechanism and is the move that made this paper foundational for everything that came after it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **WHAT THIS RECORD DOES AND DOES NOT SAY ABOUT THE REST OF THE CORPUS.** Lashley's target is the associative chain - `Watson (26) sought to identify thought with inaudible movements of the vocal organs, LINKED TOGETHER IN ASSOCIATIVE CHAINS` - and this corpus is largely built on measuring association between elements: meyer1971's free-association norms, collins1975's spreading activation, hutchison2003's association strength. **They are not the same claim.** Lashley is about the ORDER of action and speech; spreading activation is about retrieval, and retrieval has no ordering problem to solve. The honest statement is narrower and still worth holding: the corpus contains, from 1951, a sustained argument that association cannot by itself produce order - and from 1971 onward, a literature that measures association and rarely asks what orders anything

span.label: schemata of action —causes→ serial order
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — **THE SENTENCE STATES THIS AS THE PROBLEM, NOT AS A DEMONSTRATED MECHANISM, AND THE WEIGHT HAS TO CARRY THAT.** `the essential PROBLEM of serial order; the EXISTENCE of generalized schemata of action which determine the sequence` - Lashley is naming what has to exist for serial order to be possible, and the rest of the paper is an argument that nothing simpler will do. He does not show a schema; he shows that the alternatives fail. **0.85 rather than 0.95 for exactly that reason**: this is an inference to the best available explanation in 1951, presented as one, and an edge at 0.95 would read as a finding. Both endpoints are named as words and `determine` is unambiguous about direction.

span.label: Lashley argues serial order in behavior CANNOT be explained by associative chain theories (each act triggering the next); order must be centrally, hierarchically organized and imposed as a generalized pattern.
